name: Corydalis Green
lede: Corydalis Green is a pale yellow green named for corydalis, a genus of flowering plants, recorded in Ridgway's 1912 standard and repeated by Maerz and Paul in 1930.

sections.title: Named for a flowering plant
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* lists Corydalis Green on plate XLI, hue 29′′′, tone d [1]. Maerz and Paul repeat the same name in 1930, on their plate 19 B 4, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 assigns it block 122, grayish yellow green, 7.1 units from that block's centroid, a wider gap than most Ridgway names show [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-green-grey]], [[pale-green-grey]], [[pale-olive-grey]] and [[pale-olive-grey]], at 3.4, 3.4, 
Corydalis is a genus of several hundred flowering plants, many with feathery blue-green leaves, grown in gardens and found wild across the Northern Hemisphere; the color borrows the foliage's pale, slightly grey green rather than the flowers' usual yellow or pink [1]. It sits among the muted greens near [[apple-green]] and [[moss]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Corydalis Green covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 473 of them, about 2.0 per cent, as photographed [3]. It plays a highlight in 94 per cent of its appearances and peaks in paintings from the 1860s [3]. Johan Hendrik Weissenbruch is its most devoted painter here, in 3 of his 12 works, and it is comparatively frequent in Rajput painting, 7 of 97 works [3]. These are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen color, not a pigment test [3].
